output.title: Spot vendor price changes before they hit cash flow
output.body:
If you run a small business, vendor pricing changes are the kind of problem that usually show up late, on an invoice, after the amount has already shifted. The bounded workflow decision is simple: do you want to detect the change early, or keep finding it after the fact and checking the numbers by hand?

This only makes sense in a narrow setup. It fits when pricing updates or renewal notices arrive in text-based digital form, and when you already keep a baseline rate to compare against. It is not a fit for scan-heavy paperwork, and OCR-based document handling is outside our current scope. If prices rarely change, manual spot checks may be enough. No need to build software for a once-a-quarter shrug.

The control stays with you. A simple rule or extraction step can flag a change when the rate moves past a defined threshold, but the owner still decides what happens next: accept it, question it, or renegotiate. Any payment or contract change stays behind human approval.

A practical next step is to ask three questions: how often do key vendors send pricing updates, in what format do they arrive, and do you already track the baseline rates you expect to pay? If that is unclear, start there. That tells you whether this is a real workflow worth automating, or just another spreadsheet wearing a cape.
